source.extractionNote: Re-extracted after the component gained Shape=full and Flavour=inverse. Both sets read in full (6 + 54 variants) with a compact reader that reduces each difference to the axes driving it. Both metadata frames (5764:159, 5764:355) read with read-metadata. Icon glyph colour read from the nested vector's region fills in every state and style. The four on-page example instances and the Component Details card were also read.

summary: A row of mutually exclusive options sharing one track, where exactly one is active at a time. It ships with three segments, two placed directly and a third in a slot, so changing the count means working inside the instance. Use Tab Bar when the choice moves between views rather than switching a mode within one.

controls: Shape on every segment placed in the variant

intent.rounded: Match the contour of the surface the control sits on. It reaches the track and every segment placed inside it, so the whole control stays consistent without touching the items.
intent.sharp: The square-cornered pairing, for surfaces built from sharp controls.
intent.full: The pill-shaped pairing, for surfaces built from full-shaped controls.

controls: Style on the active segment placed in the variant

intent.default: Used for lighter emphasis on selected controls. Fill of the selected control subcomponent is a lighter surface on a darker grey surface parent.
intent.inverse: Used for stronger emphasis on selected controls. Fill of the selected control subcomponent is a darker surface on a lighter grey surface parent. The parent has a default-colored stroke on the border.

flavour.note: Not the segment's Flavour (default, text only, icon only): it maps to the segment's Style. The libraries expose it as an inverse switch and keep flavour for what a segment shows.

moreItems.accepts: _Segmented item only (allowPreferredValuesOnly; no min or max children; not displayed empty by default; children not stretched on insert)
moreItems.intent: Holds segments beyond the first two. It hugs its content, so whatever is placed there sets how far the track extends. (Implementation makes use of the segment options)

internalVariations.via: select into each nested _Segmented item instance
internalVariations.intent: The core surfaces none of the segment's properties. Every label, state and flavour is set by selecting into the nested instance. See the _Segmented item frame for what each one offers. (Important! In production, the core can set base properties across elements)
internalVariations.note: The metadata states the production intent: the control sets base properties (shape, style, content flavour) across all its segments, and the segments come from an options list. In Figma these are reachable only by selecting into nested instances.

contentInputs.note: State=active on one nested segment; Item 1 as shipped. The metadata requires one to always be active.

paint.border: none (default) | border/default, inside and counted in the layout (inverse)

anatomy.role: The outer frame. A horizontal auto-layout hugging its segments, carrying the background and the corner radius.

instanceProps.style: follows flavour on the active segment
instanceProps.label: Item 1, Item 2

anatomy.role: The first two segments, placed directly in the variant rather than in the slot.
The trailing region holding any further segments. It sits last in the row and hugs its content.

paint.fill: interactive/neutral/background/focused (default) | interactive/inverse/background/focused (inverse); the active segment's fill in Figma

anatomy.role: Not drawn as its own layer. The Behavior & Motion Intent says the active background is bound to the control rather than the segment and moves between items; in Figma it is the active segment's own fill.

variants._note: Shape changes only the radius token on the track and the Shape of the segments placed in the variant. Flavour changes the track fill and border and the active segment's Style. Segments a user adds to the slot are not reached (see issues).

subcomponents.name: _Segmented item
subcomponents.summary: One option inside a Segmented Control, carrying a label, an icon, or both. It is private to that control, which places two directly and a third in a slot and exposes none of its properties, so every label and state is set by selecting into the nested instance.

label.intent: The option's name. Keep it to one or two words, because segments hug their labels and a single long option makes the whole row uneven.

intent.rounded: Follow the parent control rather than deciding here. Each Segmented Control variant already sets a matching value on the segments it places.
intent.sharp: The square-cornered pairing, used where the parent is sharp.
intent.full: The pill-shaped pairing, used where the parent is full-shaped as well.

intent.default: An unchosen segment. Its label sits a step quieter than the others, which is what lets the chosen one stand out.
intent.active: The chosen segment. Exactly one in a control should carry it, and nothing in the set enforces that.
intent.hover: Pointer over an unchosen segment. It changes the label colour and adds no background, so the hover feedback is weaker here than on most controls in this system.

intent.default: Icon and label together, despite the name suggesting the plainest case. Use it when the icons add recognition the words alone do not.
intent.text only: Labels alone, and the clearest choice whenever the options are not easily iconified.
intent.icon only: Icons alone, for a control tight on space. Nothing names the options on screen, so the icons have to be unambiguous and the names supplied another way.

intent.default: The subcomponents for Segment control used within the default style parent component. Active pills have a light fill.
intent.inverse: The subcomponents for Segment control used within the inverse style parent component. Active pills have a inverse dark fill.

anatomy.role: The component frame. A horizontal auto-layout hugging its content, and the surface that carries the fill on the chosen state.

anatomy.iconSize: Icon Size=small, Framed=false (pinned by the segment)
anatomy.color: currentColor (follows the label colour; verified on the drawn vector: foreground/secondary at default, foreground/primary at hover and active, foreground/inverse at active with Style=inverse)
anatomy.role: The leading glyph, present on the default and icon only flavours.
The option's name, present on the default and text only flavours.

flavour._note: Block padding space/2xs and min-height control/sm in every flavour; measured height 36Px throughout. The gap on text only and icon only separates nothing (one child).

state._note: Style changes the active state only. Default and hover are the same in both styles.

states.changes: No fill at all. The label sits at foreground/secondary.
The label moves to foreground/primary. No background appears, so hover changes one colour and nothing else.
A fill of interactive/neutral/background/focused appears and the label moves to foreground/primary. That is the same label colour hover uses, so the fill is the only thing separating the two.

behavior.description: Figma stores no timing and no transition is authored. Becoming the chosen segment is a fill appearing, with no movement behind it.
The segment has no link to its siblings. Which one is active is decided entirely by whoever places them.

content.description: Plain text set per instance, defaulting to Item. The icon only flavour has no text node for it to reach, so the property stays settable and renders nothing.
An Icon at Size=small swapped to Star. None of its properties is exposed, so every segment shows the same glyph unless the instance is detached.
There is no second slot. A segment cannot carry a count or a badge without detaching.

do: Pick one Flavour and hold it across every segment in a control. An icon-only segment dropped into a row of labelled ones breaks the row.
Let the parent's Rounded decide the contour. Setting it per segment is how a control ends up with mismatched corners.
dont: Don't rely on hover to show what is chosen. Hover and active share a label colour, and only the fill tells them apart.
Don't use icon only without naming the options elsewhere. The glyph is a locked Star in every variant as drawn.

accessibility: No focus state exists in any of the eighteen variants, so keyboard focus has to be built entirely in code.
The chosen state is a fill plus a label-colour change. Both are colour, so the selected state has to be exposed in the markup as well.
Hover and active share foreground/primary on the label. Anyone who cannot make out the fill cannot tell the two apart.
The icon only flavour carries no text at all. Those segments need an accessible name from somewhere outside the component.
The label uses label/medium at 14px over a 20px line, and is the option's only name in two of the three flavours.

layoutTheming.description: 36 tall in all eighteen variants. Width follows the content, 80 at the default flavour, 64 at text only and 48 at icon only with the shipped label.
space/xs top and bottom throughout. Horizontally space/md on the default flavour and space/lg on both text only and icon only, so dropping a part widens the padding rather than narrowing the segment.
space/xs on the default flavour. Text only and icon only declare space/sm, which separates nothing because each has a single child.
radius/sm when true and radius/none when false.
Only active carries one, interactive/neutral/background/focused. default and hover have no fill at all.
label/medium. foreground/secondary at default, foreground/primary on both hover and active.
Icon at Size=small, 16 square, swapped to Star in every variant that shows one.

dependencies.name: Icon
dependencies.usedAs: _Segmented item icon, Size=small, Framed=false, Name swapped to Star (Style=rounded, setId 2046:10784)

tokens.extensions: companion and target override palette/primitives collections; see tokens/manifest.json
tokens._note: All 21 bound variable names resolve in tokens/base/** (semantics, size, typography); the label/medium text style is bound to its five typography variables. The glyph star (setId 2046:10784) is in packages/icons/codepoints.json, not retired, and not in inventory.json's rejected list. One gap: the inverse track's border weight is a raw value (see issues). The export has no duration or easing tokens, so the metadata's motion timing has no token to name.

control.changes: The core declares no state axis of its own. Which segment looks chosen is set on the nested items.

control.trigger: State set to active on one segment
control.changes: That segment gains a fill and its label moves to the primary foreground. Nothing in the core enforces that only one carries it.

states._note: Per-segment states (default, hover, active) live on _Segmented item, in both styles. No focus, pressed or disabled state exists on either set.

behavior.description: The active background moves in 0.15s ease-in transition between item in the control. (Active background is not tied to the segmented item but bound to the control, so it moves easily across items)
The set ships with Item 1 active, there most always be an active segment on.
The count is structural rather than a property. Two segments sit directly in each variant and a third in the slot, so a fourth means duplicating inside the instance. (Figma only implementation)

content.description: Holds segments beyond the first two. It hugs its content, so whatever is placed there sets how far the track extends. (Implementation makes use of the segment options)

content.type: two placed instances, outside the slot
content.description: Item 1 and Item 2 are placed directly in each variant rather than in the slot. Removing one means detaching, and Item 1 is the one shipped active. (Figma only)

The core surfaces none of the segment's properties. Every label, state and flavour is set by selecting into the nested instance. See the _Segmented item frame for what each one offers. (Important! In production, the core can set base properties across elements)

do: Keep the options short and parallel. The row is read in one glance, so uneven label lengths make the track look broken.
Set exactly one segment to active. The component will not do it, and will happily show two.
dont: Don't use it to move between screens. It switches a mode within one view, which is what separates it from Tab Bar.
Don't grow it past a handful of segments. Each one hugs its own label, so a long list pushes the track wider than whatever contains it.

accessibility: The control is one choice among several. It needs a radiogroup or tablist role rather than a row of unrelated buttons.
No focus state exists on the core or on the segments, so arrow-key movement and a visible focus ring both have to come from code.
The chosen segment is shown by a fill and a text-colour change. Expose the selected state in the markup rather than leaving it to colour.

The track uses interactive/neutral/background/pressed and the active segment interactive/neutral/background/focused. Check those two against each other, because the difference between chosen and unchosen is the whole point of the control.
Nothing prevents two segments reading as active at once. That has to be enforced, or the control contradicts itself.

layoutTheming.description: 289 by 44 as shipped with three segments. Width follows the segments, so it grows with their labels.
space/xs on all four sides of the track, with a space/xs gap between segments.
radius/sm when true and radius/none when false, on the track and on every segment it places.
interactive/neutral/background/pressed on the track. No border and no shadow.
Each segment hugs its own content, so the track is the sum of the labels rather than an equal-width grid. Segments are not the same width as each other.
The More items Slot hugs whatever is placed in it and sits last in the row.

pageExamples.note: Slot segments 3 and 4 are Shape=rounded inside a sharp control.
Slot segments 3 and 4 are Shape=rounded inside a full control.

visualReference.policy: No images are stored; every node deep-links into Figma so a shot can be pulled on demand and is never stale.

issues.detail: Behavior & Motion Intent now says the active background is bound to the control and moves between items with a 0.15s ease-in transition. Nothing on the canvas models that: the fill is the active segment's own (State=active), there is no indicator layer on the track, and neither set has prototype reactions. Build it as one control-level indicator using interactive/neutral/background/focused and the segment's radius.

The control's Motion row (0.15s ease-in, moving background) contradicts the _Segmented item's Motion row ('Figma stores no timing and no transition is authored. Becoming the chosen segment is a fill appearing, with no movement behind it.'). The control-level text is newer and more specific; the segment frame was not updated.
The More items Slot property is not in the Property Breakdown table; it appears only under Content & Slot.

Layout & Theming says horizontal padding is 'space/md on the default flavour'. Only the start side is: the default flavour binds paddingLeft space/md and paddingRight space/lg (asymmetric). Text only and icon only are space/lg on both sides.
The metadata now says space/xs for the track's padding and gap and for the segment's block padding and default gap. Figma binds space/2xs in all four places.

Only the Property Breakdown covers inverse. States, Layout & Theming and Accessibility still describe the default flavour alone, so the inverse track fill, border, active fill and foreground/inverse label come from the bindings.
The inverse track's border weight is a raw 1 with no stroke token bound. stroke/thin carries the same value.
In Shape=full, Flavour=default the slot's segment is Shape=sharp, so one segment has square corners inside a pill track. Every other variant matches its segments to the Shape.
The control's Flavour (default, inverse) and the segment's Flavour (default, text only, icon only) share a name but are different choices. The control's Flavour corresponds to the segment's Style.

Both Layout & Theming Radius rows still read 'radius/sm when true and radius/none when false' and name no value for full. The segment's Usage still says 'Let the parent's Rounded decide', and its text still counts 'eighteen variants' where there are now 54.

No focus state on either set, and no pressed or disabled state on the segment, in either flavour. Focus ring, keyboard (arrow-key) movement and any disabled treatment have no Figma design and no token guidance; code must choose them.

The icon is locked to the star glyph in all 54 variants with no exposed swap, so default and icon only flavours cannot show a meaningful icon as drawn. With 'Implementation makes use of the segment options', the glyph becomes a per-option input in code.

The sharp examples (5757:827, 5757:857) and the full example (5757:853) hold slot segments at Shape=rounded. Shape reaches only the three segments placed in the variant; segments added to the slot keep their own value, contradicting 'It reaches the track and every segment placed inside it'.

The metadata's 0.15s ease-in has no token. By owner decision the indicator uses the animations/spring token instead (size collection, "250ms cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.36, 0.64, 1)", added 2026-10-21), the same motion as Switch.

Selection intent is now explicit: 'there most always be an active segment on' (verbatim; reads as 'must always'). The structure still allows two or none, and the Usage Do and Accessibility text still say the component won't enforce it, so code must enforce exactly one.

The metadata now marks the fixed two-plus-slot structure and the 'Adding segments' duplication as Figma-only, says the slot maps to segment options in implementation, and says in production the core can set base properties (shape, flavour) across segments. This settles the earlier open decision: an options list plus control-level shape and flavour.
Size is described as 'fixed height'; in Figma the segment hugs vertically with min-height bound to control/sm (36 measured). Same result at the shipped content.
Hover and active share foreground/primary on the label; hover adds no fill. Only the active fill separates them (the metadata flags this itself).
Text only and icon only bind gap space/sm with a single child, so the gap has no effect.
The Label property stays settable on icon only but has no text node to reach; icon only segments need an accessible name from outside.
More items Slot allows preferred values only (_Segmented item), with no min or max children, not displayed empty by default and no stretch on insert.

Icon colour is not a token on the segment: the drawn vector's region fill follows the label (foreground/secondary, then foreground/primary on hover and active). A font glyph with currentColor satisfies this.
Neither component set has a Figma description. Motion is described for the control (see above) but not authored in Figma.

The inverse variants label the first segment 'Item' rather than 'Item 1', and only Shape=full sets Style=inverse on an unchosen segment. Neither changes the look, because Style affects the active state only.
Icon family is pinned to rounded in all 54 variants, including Shape=sharp. Shape does not switch the glyph family.
Contrast between the track and the active segment is not verified here for either flavour; the metadata asks for the default pair to be checked and does not mention the inverse pair.
Of the four on-page examples, 5757:857 duplicates 5757:827. The Component Details card lists Web as 'Pending development'.
